key_insight: The paper shifts the focus from what Transformers can represent to what they can actually learn, proposing preliminary sample-complexity bounds for learning narrow-teacher C-RASP constructions.
engineering_relevance: This matters for LLM engineering because it helps distinguish theoretically expressible Transformer behaviors from those that are realistically learnable with finite data and optimization.
method: Analyze Transformer learnability through the C-RASP formalism.
Use handcrafted-weight constructions and computational-complexity-inspired arguments.
Derive preliminary sample-complexity bounds informed by loss-landscape analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical study with preliminary sample-complexity bounds, rather than reporting a benchmark dataset or empirical evaluation.
watch_item: The results are preliminary and theoretical, so the bounds may not directly predict practical training behavior for large-scale Transformers.
paper_title: From Expressivity to Sample Complexity: Narrow Teachers for Transformers via C-RASP
